questions.question: In which of the following years was the Food Corporation of India (FCI) set up?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __1965__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

Food Corporation of India:

 
• The Food Corporation of India is an organisation under the government of India.
 
• It was set up under the Food Corporation act in 1964.
 
• It was thus established in the year 1965.
 
• The key objectives of the Food Corporation of India are:
 
 
• Ensuring that farmers are not forced to sell their produce below MSP by providing effective price support operations.
 
• Setting up purchase centres to buy produce from the farmers.
 
• Distribution of food grains throughout the country for the public distribution system.
 
• Maintaining a satisfactory level of operational and buffer stocks of foodgrains to ensure National Food Security.
 
• To intervene in the market for price stabilization.
 
 
 
• The headquarters of the food corporation of India is in New Delhi.
 
• The Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food, and Public Distribution is the parent organisation of the food corporation of India.
 
• 
 
Thus, the Food Corporation of India was established in the year 1965.

questions.question: The word monsoon refers to __________.

options.text: blowing of wind in one direction always

questions.solution:
• Monsoon is defined as the changing direction of winds accompanied by constant changes in the precipitation of the atmosphere causing the formation of a season reversing wind.
 
• A storm is an example of a monsoon wind that is responsible for heavy flood and other damages.

questions.question: Which of the following cities is NOT situated on the bank of river Ganga?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lucknow**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** The Ganga System

 
• The Ganga is the most important river in India both from the point of view of its basin and cultural significance.
 
• It rises in the Gangotri glacier near Gaumukh (3,900 m) in the Uttarkashi district of Uttarakhand. Here, it is known as the Bhagirathi.
 
• It cuts through the Central and the Lesser Himalayas in narrow gorges.
 
• At Devprayag, the Bhagirathi meets the Alaknanda; hereafter, it is known as the Ganga.
 
• The Alaknanda has its source in the Satopanth glacier above Badrinath.
 
 
• The Alaknanda consists of the Dhauli and the Vishnu Ganga which meet at Joshimath or Vishnu Prayag.
 
• The other tributaries of Alaknanda such as the Pindar join it at Karna Prayag while Mandakini or Kali Ganga meets it at Rudra Prayag.
 
 
 
• The Ganga enters the plains at Haridwar. From here, it flows first to the south, then to the southeast and east before splitting into two distributaries, namely the Bhagirathi and the Padma.
 
• The river has a length of 2,525 km.
 
• It is shared by Uttarakhand (110 km) and Uttar Pradesh (1,450 km), Bihar (445 km), and West Bengal (520 km).
 
• The Son is its major right-bank tributary.
 
• The important left-bank tributaries are the Ramganga, the Gomati, the Ghaghara, the Gandak, the Kosi, and the Mahananda.
 
• The river finally discharges itself into the Bay of Bengal near Sagar Island.

questions.question: Bohr’s model is related to which of the following?

options.text: The concept of quantization of energy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The concept of quantization of energy.**__

__**Explanation:**__

 
• Bohr’s model was presented by Niels Bohr and Ernest Rutherford in 1913 and is related to the concept of quantization of energy.
 
• According to the concept the atom is defined as a system consisting of a dense nucleus surrounded by revolving electrons.
 
• The Bohr model of the atom was put forth by Neil Bohr in 1915.
 
• According to this idea, negatively charged electrons in an atom move in defined circular orbits or shells that encircle the positively charged nucleus.
 
• - The energy of each orbit or shell is known.
 
• - The energy levels are denoted by the quantum number =1,2,3, etc. ), which is an integer. The nucleus side, which has the lowest energy level, is where this quantum number range starts.
 
• - The electrons of an atom can move from a lower energy level to a higher energy level by receiving the required energy, and from a higher energy level to a lower energy level by losing energy.
 
• Ernest Rutherford, a British scientist, conducted an experiment, and based on the findings, he suggested the atomic structure of the elements and developed the Rutherford Atomic Model (1911). The Thomson atomic model was developed in 1900, while the Bohr model of the atom was first proposed in 1915. As a result, it is the wrong choice.

questions.question:
Which among the following comes under Union List of Indian Constitution?

I. Defense

II. Inter-state Trade and Commerce

III. Banking
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**All I, II, and III**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Union List, also known as List-I, is a list of **100 items** that were given in the **7th schedule** in the Indian Constitution.
 
• Defense, Banking, and Inter-State Trade and Commerce all come under this list.
 
• **SEVENTH SCHEDULE (Article 246) List I—Union List**
 
• 1. **Defense** of India and every part thereof including preparation for defense and all such acts as may be conducive in times of war to its prosecution and after its termination to effective demobilization.
 
• 42. **Inter-State trade and commerce.**
 
• 43. Incorporation, regulation, and winding up of trading corporations, including banking, insurance, and financial corporations, but not including co-operative societies.
 
• 45. **Banking**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• State List: States have exclusive powers on this list to deal with.

 
 
• Public order, Railways Police, Public health and sanitation, Prisons, reformatories, Borstal institutions, and other institutions of a like nature, etc
 
 
 
• Concurrent List: Both Union and States can make laws on the subjects in this list.
 
 
• Bankruptcy and insolvency, Trust and Trustees, Prevention of cruelty to animals, etc.

questions.question: In India, Financial Emergency can be extended for what maximum duration?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Indefinite period**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Financial Emergency**

 
 
• **Grounds of declaration**: Article 360 empowers the president to proclaim a Financial Emergency if he is satisfied that a situation has arisen due to which the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened.
 
• **Parliamentary approval and duration**: A proclamation declaring financial emergency must be approved by both the Houses of Parliament within two months from the date of its issue.
 
 
• If the proclamation of Financial Emergency is issued at a time when the Lok Sabha has been dissolved or the dissolution of the Lok Sabha takes place during the period of two months without approving the proclamation, then the proclamation survives until 30 days from the first sitting of the Lok Sabha after its reconstitution, provided the Rajya Sabha has in the meantime approved it.
 
• **Once approved by both the houses of Parliament, the Financial Emergency continues indefinitely till it is revoked.**

questions.question: Which meristem increases the length of the stems and the roots?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Apical Meristem__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Apical Meristem** increases the length of the roots and stem as it produces auxin which is a plant hormone.
 
• It can be found at the tips of the shoot and root of a plant.
 
• The actual apical meristem is a** cluster of densely packed and undifferentiated cells. **
 
• In the shoot apical meristem, cells are only created in **one direction. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lateral meristem**

 
 
• Plants use** lateral meristem tissue to grow in diameter **as part of secondary growth.
 
• There are two types of lateral meristematic tissue—**the vascular cambium and the cork cambium.**
 
 
 
• **Intercalary meristem**
 
 
• The intercalary tissue in the middle of the plant is **capable of rapid growth and regrowth**.
 
• The intercalary tissue at the base of a** blade of grass allows it to regrow **after being cut.

questions.question: Calculate the time period (in seconds) of a sound wave of wavelength 3 m traveling with a speed of 300 m/s.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.01.**__

**__Calculation:__**

Here, the velocity (v) = 300 m/s and wavelength = 3 m. Therefore, the frequency = 300/3 = 100 (f).

Now the time period = 1/100 = **0.01**

questions.question: ___________ constitute the biotic component of the biosphere.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Living things.**__

__**Explanation:**__

 
• Both biotic and abiotic elements are present in ecosystems.
 
• Biotic Components: 
 
 
• Biotic Components are the living things that shape an ecosystem.
 
• It includes producers, consumers, and decomposers.
 
• All living things have a direct or indirect influence on other organisms in an environment.
 
• Example: plants, animals, humans, microorganisms etc.
 
 
 
• Abiotic Components:
 
 
• Abiotic Components are non-living components that influence the ecosystem.
 
• In biology and ecology, abiotic components and variables refer to non-living chemical and physical elements of the environment that have an effect on living things and the health of ecosystems.
 
• Example: Air, water, soil, etc.
 
 

​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/23f3ce16c75a0a2a6f83bdcfed2dc94416187bfaf3bfeef3290dd519fb524d4a.png]

• First developed by Tim Berners-Lee in 1990, HTML is short for Hypertext Markup Language.
 
• HTML is used to create electronic documents (called pages) that are displayed on the World Wide Web.
 
• It is a language used for writing source codes for developing a webpage, inserting content, and other components in it.
 
• HTML is a markup language because it is used to distinguish HTML elements from the text.
 
• HTML is not a programming language, meaning it doesn’t have the ability to create dynamic functionality. Instead, it makes it possible to organize and format documents, similar to Microsoft Word.
 
• When working with HTML, we use simple code structures (tags and attributes) to mark up a website page. For example, we can create a paragraph by placing the enclosed text within a starting *
